# Best time to run

> besttimetorun.com finds the best weather window for a run today and tomorrow: give it a location and the hours you
> can run, and it returns the driest, calmest, most comfortable stretch for each run length from 15 minutes to 3 hours,
> with the wind direction to start into. Free, anonymous, no account or key. Weather from Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0).

The page at https://besttimetorun.com/ does this for a GPX/KML route (read in the browser, never uploaded) or the
device's location. Everything it shows comes from the public JSON API below.

## API

- [OpenAPI contract](https://besttimetorun.com/openapi.yaml): the full description of both endpoints.
- `GET https://besttimetorun.com/api/window?lat=52.37&lon=4.89&avail=07-09,12-14,17-21`: the best window per run
  length for today and tomorrow, as UTC ISO times. `lat` and `lon` are rounded to 2 decimals (about 1 km). Optional:
  `dark` (`avoid` or `ok`), `rain` (highest chance of rain allowed, %), `prefer` (`balanced`, `wind`, `rain` or
  `temp`), `slots=1` (every 15-minute slot with its weather and score).
- `GET https://besttimetorun.com/api/capacity`: how much of today's cap of new locations is left.

## MCP

- `https://besttimetorun.com/mcp`: a stateless MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no sign-in) for AI assistants. Tools:
  `find_best_run_time` (latitude, longitude, minutes, day `today` or `tomorrow`, and optional `hours`, `darkOk`,
  `maxRainChance`, `mindMost`) returns the best stretch with its local times, conditions and which way to start;
  `get_run_conditions` returns the day's 15-minute slots. Ask the user for their town if you don't know it.
  Hosts that show MCP Apps draw `find_best_run_time`'s answer with the day's timeline (`ui://besttimetorun/day.html`).
- A first prompt: "Using Best time to run, when is the best time today for a 45-minute run near Utrecht? I can run
  07–09 or 17–21. I mind the wind most."

## Limits

- At most 300 distinct locations per UTC day; a location already asked for keeps working all day.
- A per-client rate limit per second (HTTP 429 with Retry-After).
- Please call it for real runs, not to collect forecasts in bulk: it shares Open-Meteo's free quota.

## Optional

- [Source code](https://github.com/axtg/run-window): the API, this page and a TRMNL e-paper plugin.
